patterns.usage_note: Marks a special, milestone-like occasion (開店[かいてん], 就任[しゅうにん], 卒業[そつぎょう]) and the deliberate step you take as it approaches, so the main clause is typically something planned rather than something that just happens. It attaches to a noun or to a verb in dictionary form. Its drier sibling に際[さい]して attaches the same way; the difference is register and occasion type, not attachment — にあたって leans toward welcome milestones you prepare for, に際して toward the bare moment an event occurs, including unwelcome ones. It is formal enough for speeches and written notices; in ordinary conversation 〜とき or 〜前[まえ]に does the same work. にあたり is the clipped written shape, にあたっての the form used before a noun.

examples.ruby: 新[あたら]しい店[みせ]を開[ひら]くにあたって、資金[しきん]を集[あつ]めた。
examples.english: In preparation for opening the new shop, we raised the funds.

examples.ruby: 留学[りゅうがく]するにあたって、先輩[せんぱい]に相談[そうだん]した。
examples.english: Before going to study abroad, I went to an upperclassman for advice.

examples.ruby: 新人[しんじん]を採用[さいよう]するにあたって、基準[きじゅん]を決[き]めた。
examples.english: Before taking on new hires, we settled on our criteria.

patterns.usage_note: Very close to にあたって, but drier and more bureaucratic: it points at the moment a specific event actually takes place and at what that moment calls for. It is most often built on a noun (使用[しよう]に際[さい]して), though a dictionary-form verb is grammatical too (署名[しょめい]するに際して); the clipped に際し is the standard shape in manuals and public notices. It takes unwelcome or emergency occasions (非常時[ひじょうじ]に際して) more readily than にあたって, which leans toward happy milestones.

examples.ruby: 退職[たいしょく]に際[さい]して、社長[しゃちょう]から花束[はなたば]を頂[いただ]いた。
examples.english: On leaving the company, I was presented with a bouquet by the president.

examples.ruby: 非常時[ひじょうじ]に際[さい]しては、係員[かかりいん]の指示[しじ]に従[したが]ってください。
examples.english: In the event of an emergency, please follow the staff's instructions.

examples.ruby: 契約書[けいやくしょ]に署名[しょめい]するに際[さい]し、条項[じょうこう]を読[よ]み上[あ]げた。
examples.english: At the signing of the contract, the clauses were read aloud.

patterns.usage_note: Frames an entire surrounding condition or sphere (この不況[ふきょう]にあって, 戦後[せんご]の混乱[こんらん]にあって) rather than a point in time, and the main clause says what holds true inside it. It is stiffer than において or で and belongs to writing, speeches, and narration. にあっては tends to set the sphere against some other one (会社[かいしゃ]では厳[きび]しいが家庭[かてい]にあっては…), and にあっても means "even in". において locates an event in a place or domain; にあって places a subject inside a condition and then says how they fare there. Nouns only.

examples.ruby: この不況[ふきょう]にあって、社員[しゃいん]の給与[きゅうよ]は据[す]え置[お]きだ。
examples.english: In a slump like this one, employee pay is being held where it is.

examples.ruby: 戦後[せんご]の混乱[こんらん]にあって、人々[ひとびと]は助[たす]け合[あ]った。
examples.english: Amid the chaos of the postwar years, people looked after one another.

examples.ruby: 父[ちち]は職場[しょくば]では厳[きび]しいが、家庭[かてい]にあっては無口[むくち]な人[ひと]だった。
examples.english: My father was stern at work, but at home he was a man of few words.
